title: What setup and an edit may save: a schedule change never before its latest settled or named occurrence, a goal's own account in the home currency, setup's not-yet questions (X8, W3, X3)
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 sections 4, 5 and 8 (the opening); DECISIONS_ROUND2 X3, X8, W3, AB3 (the last statement asked at setup; AD6 and AD7: "no" asks the amount with everything owed filled in, "don't know" on a loan or pay-later is that month's usual payment) and AB with MAKO M1 (the minimum asked once, box empty)
notes: Hand-worked cases for edit-time and setup rules that the reference model does not hold [H7]. All amounts and dates are made up.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: A pay day change dated before a settled pay is refused; the edit offers the day after it (X8, c8)
cases.why: The latest settled occurrence of the pay is pay@2026-12-10 (rent's settle is another schedule's). 1 Dec is on or before it, so the change would rename or remove a settled pay [X8]: refused, and the edit offers Fri 11 Dec, the first day after it.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: A change dated after every settled pay is saved as asked (X8)
cases.why: 1 Jan 2027 is after pay@2026-12-10, the latest settled occurrence, so nothing settled or named is rewritten [X8, H2].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: A change dated on the settled occurrence's own due date is refused (X8)
cases.why: On or before: a change from 10 Dec would own the 10 Dec occurrence [H2], so it is refused and 11 Dec offered [X8].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: An occurrence named by `amounts` counts, even when not settled (X8)
cases.why: `amounts` names pay@2027-01-10 (keyed by its due date). A change from 5 Jan would make that key name nothing [X8]: refused, 11 Jan offered.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: Periods named by the pay (`pe:` and `ps:`) count (X8, T1)
cases.why: The period-end answer names pay@2027-01-10 and the period start stands in for pay@2027-02-10 [T1]. The latest is 10 Feb, so a change from 1 Feb is refused and 11 Feb offered [X8].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: A one-period override (`once`) keyed by a pay counts (X8)
cases.why: A budget line's `once` is keyed pay@2027-03-10 [T1]; a change from 1 Mar would leave it naming nothing [X8].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: Only the changed schedule's own occurrences count (X8)
cases.why: The rent's latest settled occurrence is rent@2026-11-27; the pay's settle and the period named by the pay are another schedule's. 1 Dec is after 27 Nov, so the rent change is saved [X8].

cases.question: own_account
cases.title: A goal's money moved to its own account in the home currency is allowed (W3, V1)
cases.why: The account is in yen, the home currency [W3].

cases.question: own_account
cases.title: A goal's own account in another currency is stage 2 (W3)
cases.why: In version one a goal's own account must be in the home currency; a peso account for a yen home is stage 2 [W3].

cases.question: own_account
cases.title: After a change of home currency the new home currency is the one checked (W3, O6)
cases.why: The home currency in force is pesos [O6], so a peso account may back a goal [W3].

cases.question: not_yet_asks
cases.title: Setup asks about pay and bills due from the last pay to the setup day, a pay due that day first (X3, F20)
cases.why: Asked: what is due after the last pay (25 May, already in) up to and including the setup day, Fri 25 Jun [X3]. The pay due that day is asked first; the rest by due date. Rent of 27 Jun is after setup and is simply expected.

cases.question: not_yet_asks
cases.title: Nothing due since the last pay: setup asks nothing (X3)
cases.why: Nothing is due between the last pay and the setup day, so there is nothing to ask [X3].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: a card set up between its close and its payment day is asked "Is the last statement paid?"; yes is saved as a paid statement
cases.why: The card closes on the last day and is paid on the 27th of the next month. Setup on Fri 20 Nov falls after the close of Sat 31 Oct and before its payment day, Fri 27 Nov, so setup asks [AB3]. Yes: a statement check for the 31 Oct close, paid; no amount is asked. Everything owed now is after that close.

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3, AD6: answered no: the amount box opens with everything owed filled in; the person types the statement's amount
cases.why: No, not paid: setup asks the amount with everything owed, 50,000, filled in [AD6]; the person changes it to the October statement, 30,000: saved as an unpaid statement closed 31 Oct and paid 27 Nov [AB3, J5]. Of the 50,000 owed, 50,000 - 30,000 = 20,000 is November so far.

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: answered don't know: everything owed is that statement, due on the next payment day
cases.why: "Don't know" counts everything owed as due on the next payment day [AB3]: the statement saved holds all 50,000 owed and is paid on Fri 27 Nov (the safe side, as H4).

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: set up after the payment day and before the next close: not asked (X6 holds)
cases.why: Sat 28 Nov is after the 27 Nov payment day of the October statement and before the next close, Mon 30 Nov. There is no statement waiting between its close and its payment day, so nothing is asked; the first close after the opening holds what is owed [X6].

cases.question: min_ask
cases.title: Mako M1: setup asks "Keep at least ___ in your bank?" with the box empty; skipping means no minimum
cases.why: The box starts empty (no amount filled in for the person) and they skip it: `home.minBank` is null, no minimum [AB, MAKO M1].

cases.question: min_ask
cases.title: Mako M1: a typed minimum is kept in the home currency
cases.why: The person types 20,000: `home.minBank` is { a: 20,000, cur: JPY } [AB, MAKO M1, O6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD6: answered no and the filled-in amount left as it is: everything owed is that statement
cases.why: No, not paid: the amount box opens with everything owed, 50,000 [AD6]. The person leaves it, so the unpaid statement closed Sat 31 Oct holds 50,000, all due on Fri 27 Nov; 50,000 - 50,000 = 0 is November so far. Before AD6 a "no" with no amount typed saved no amount (ed-q1).

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD7: a loan answered don't know: that month's usual payment is due on the next payment day, not the whole balance
cases.why: A loan of 400,000 paying 20,000 a month on the 27th, set up Fri 20 Nov, between its statement (Sat 31 Oct) and its payment day (Fri 27 Nov), so setup asks [AB3]. "Don't know" on a loan means that month's usual payment, 20,000, is due on Fri 27 Nov [AD7], not the whole 400,000 owed. 400,000 - 20,000 = 380,000 stays owed after it.

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD7: a pay-later answered don't know: that month's usual payment
cases.why: A pay-later owing 30,000, paying 10,000 a month on the 27th, set up Fri 20 Nov: "don't know" means that month's usual payment, 10,000, is due on Fri 27 Nov [AD7]; 30,000 - 10,000 = 20,000 stays owed.

open.question: AD6: "No, not paid" asks the amount with everything owed filled in. On a loan or a pay-later (everything owed is the whole balance, 400,000 on a loan paying 20,000 a month), is the amount asked too, and filled with what: everything owed, or that month's usual payment (as AD7 reads "don't know")?
open.ref_does: AD6 only on a card. A loan or pay-later answered no saves the amount typed, with no box filled (the AB3 reading: "no" leaves that payment expected, its usual amount, loan_between_stmt_pay lbs-01). No case has it.
